accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE 2013 GCSE Mathematics subject content A18 (solve quadratic equations algebraically by factorising) and Common Core A-SSE.3.a and A-REI.4.b. Every worked equation was verified by substitution: (x + 4)(x − 3) = 0 gives −4 and 3 and both satisfy x² + x = 12; x(x − 5) = 0 gives 0 and 5 for x² = 5x; (x − 2)(x − 3) = 6 is solved by 0 and 5 (−2 × −3 = 6 and 3 × 2 = 6), while 8 and 9 give 30 and 42; 2x − 1 = 0 gives ½ and 3x + 4 = 0 gives −4/3. Parameterised items were checked across their full ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors in solving quadratics by factorising: sign errors on roots (prediction x = 4 and x = −1, tag sign, and the Signs flipped message on the graph), factorising before rearranging to 0 (prediction Factorise: x(x + 1) = 12, tag notzero, and the whole Why it must be 0 step), dividing by x and losing the root 0 (Divide by x tile refused with a check, tag divide), giving one root (tag one), confusing x² = 7x with x² = 7 (tag root) and ignoring the coefficient in 2x − 3 = 0 (prediction x = 1 or x = 2, tag coef).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagzprod is a zero-product model: a number-line slider drives two bracket values and their product, root dots are dragged on the x-axis to rebuild y = (x − a)(x − b), method tiles enforce rearrange, factorise, set each factor = 0, a slider tests (x − 2)(x − 3) = 6 against the line y = 6, and root chips are matched to linear factors with coefficients. flagfact (algebra tiles for factorising) and flagsqroot (y = k against y = x²) share no mechanic, and the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the reason before reading it: the product card turns green only when a bracket card shows 0, the curve crosses the axis exactly at the dragged roots, the Factorise tile is refused on x² + x = 12 with the 3 × 4 example, the graph shows x = 8 giving 30 rather than 6 while 0 and 5 land on the orange line, and wrong root chips are tested by substitution. Done messages state the rule only after the evidence is on screen.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions with tempting wrong options that the lab then tests: One or None for (x − 2)(x + 5) = 0 (the slider finds two), x = 4 and x = −1 (the dots must go to −4 and 1), Factorise: x(x + 1) = 12 (refused), Yes: x = 8 for (x − 2)(x − 3) = 6 (gives 30), and x = 1 or x = 2 for 2x − 1 = 0 (gives ½). A.reveal repeats the learner's pick next to the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions (bracket form, x² = 7x, a trinomial, x(x − 4) = 5, and a factor with coefficient 2) with every wrong answer tagged to a specific message: sign, one, divide, root, factor (the multiply-to and add-to pair), notzero (rearranged form shown) and coef. Option order rotates so the right answer is not always first.

readability.evidence: Learner audience for ages 14 to 16: kid paragraphs use short sentences with one worked example each and pass the learner kid limit; adult paragraphs use the exact terms zero product property, root, solution, standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, common factor and the A18, A-SSE.3.a and A-REI.4.b references, and pass the learner adult limit. Lab tiles are two to four words (Rearrange to = 0, Factorise, Set each factor = 0, Divide by x).

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with Factorising x² + bx + c and Solving quadratics by square roots is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (the rule, brackets and signs with the graph link, factorising first with a check, rearranging and the divide-by-x trap plus coefficients); adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, key terms, six named mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark after every Show me: the three bracket cards fit in one row with 30 px values, the number line labels every even number, root dots are 11 px with a 40 px vertical grab band, the method lines and their reasons sit apart above two rows of tiles, the graph labels do not cover the curve, and the four factor rows and six chips fit without clipping. Every canvas action has a full-width button twin.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge appeared. Sliding, root moves, method steps and matching all work by buttons (x + 1, Purple ▶, Pick ½ then Put in 2x − 1 = 0), the aria-label speaks each result (x = 2: x − 2 = 0, so the product is 0) and matches are shown with text as well as colour.
